title: Saviour, Breathe an Evening Blessing
description: Saviour, Breathe an Evening Blessing in Tonic Solfa to EVENING PRAYER (STEBBINS): the solfa with the words, staff notation, the four verses, and a piano.
about: James Edmeston’s words appeared in his Sacred Lyrics in 1820. George C. Stebbins wrote the tune EVENING PRAYER in 1878.
underlay: Sa-viour, breathe an eve-ning bless-ing, Ere re-pose our_ spi-rits_ seal_; Sin and want we come con-fess-ing; Thou canst save, and Thou canst heal.

lines: Sin and want we come confessing;
Thou canst save, and Thou canst heal.
Tho’ the arrows past us fly,
Angel guards from Thee surround us,
We are safe if Thou art nigh.
Tho’ the night be dark and dreary,
Thou art He who, never weary,
Should swift death this night o’ertake us,
And our couch become our tomb,
May the morn in heaven awake us,
Clad in bright and deathless bloom.
